remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation actually includes the Spanish-language billing limitation.
No admissible evidence shows an approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance for the material segment weakness.
The Spanish-language billing subgroup remains below threshold for a named launch use case.
Prior approval is stale contextual evidence and cannot satisfy the current-release requirement after the locale-routing update and new eval batch.
Informal post-launch monitoring does not satisfy the policy requirement for approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance.
final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and relied on a narrower interpretation of the same record. That reinterpretation usefully concedes that aggregate readiness, no severity-one rehearsal incidents, prior approval, and informal monitoring are not enough by themselves. But the governing policy is conditional: certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by an approved mitigation. On the available record, there is still no admissible evidence of attached current-release disclosure language, approved mitigation, or formal risk acceptance for the Spanish-language billing regression. A caveated description of the weakness in the audit packet summary is not the same as evidence that the required release materials satisfy the policy predicate. Because the unresolved compliance condition remains unmet on the admissible record, the claim that the current release can be certified now remains noncompliant.
